diagnosis: The FIFO emits three extra valid cycles (13–15) after the input window ends at cycle 13, indicating that the read pointer or the output-valid latch is not being cleared when the frame is dropped or the FIFO becomes empty. The extra assertions occur because mem_read_data_valid_reg retains a stale ‘1’ after the last accepted frame, so the output stage continues to drive m_axis_tvalid high even though no new data has been written.

ranking.mechanism: s_axis_tready is incorrectly gated by rst, allowing write-side logic to run during reset and leaving drop_frame_reg asserted, which prevents wr_ptr_cur from rewinding and leaves a phantom frame in the FIFO.

s_axis_tready is qualified with !rst, blocking legitimate writes after reset release and causing the write pointer to stall while the read side drains the FIFO, leaving mem_read_data_valid_reg stuck high.

The drop-frame condition is gated by !s_axis_tready, so when the downstream de-asserts tready the condition falsely fires, setting drop_frame_next and preventing wr_ptr_cur from advancing to the frame boundary.

good_frame_next defaults to good_frame_reg instead of 1’b0, so a previously asserted good_frame_reg remains high and masks the overflow/bad-frame status that would otherwise clear the output valid latch.
bad_frame_next defaults to bad_frame_reg, causing a stale bad-frame flag to persist and interfere with the drop-frame/rewind logic that should clear the read side.
overflow_next defaults to overflow_reg, making the overflow status sticky and preventing the internal full/empty comparison from resetting the read-pointer valid flag after a dropped frame.
